title: Tree zigzag nerves are filtered colimits over finite subtrees
statement:
Let $T$ be a small oriented tree: its underlying undirected graph is nonempty and has a unique finite simple path between any two vertices, and each edge is assigned one direction. Let $C_T$ be its free path category, whose arrows are finite composable directed edge words and whose identities are empty words. For a finite word $w$ in $+,-$, let $Z_w^{C_T}(x,y)$ have the meaning of [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus] for the pair $(C_T,C_T)$; identity horizontal arrows are allowed. Fix a vertex $x$. Let $\mathcal F_x(T)$ be the poset of finite connected subtrees $S\subseteq T$ containing $x$, ordered by inclusion, including the singleton subtree $\{x\}$. This is a small nonempty filtered category. Subtree inclusions induce degreewise injective maps between the nerves of the fixed-word zigzag categories. The resulting canonical map is an isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$\varinjlim_{S\in\mathcal F_x(T)}NZ_w^{C_S}(x,x)\ \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\ NZ_w^{C_T}(x,x).$$
Here the colimit is computed degreewise in sets as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
